html:
Cyrenaica is the eastern region of Libya, named after the ancient Greek city of Cyrene. The map shows it as its own unit from 1715 to 1815, when it was governed from Benghazi as part of the Karamanli state of Tripolitania.

Its green coastal uplands, the Jebel Akhdar, made it the most fertile part of Libya. Greeks from Thera founded Cyrene around 631 BCE, and the region later belonged to the Ptolemies and to Rome. After the Arab conquest it was called Barqa. Under the Ottomans it was a thinly peopled land of Bedouin tribes, with Benghazi its main port.

In the 1800s the Senussi Sufi order built lodges across Cyrenaica and became its real government. When Italy invaded in 1911, the Senussi led the resistance; their best-known fighter was Omar Mukhtar, hanged in 1931. The Senussi leader Idris became king of an independent Libya in 1951.
